title: Request shaper and deferred prefetch playbook for GPU pool stabilization
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: During a sustained traffic spike on 2026-02-12, multiple hosted GPU pools experienced progressive queue buildup followed by rapid admission throttling that caused elevated tail latency and a 23% increase in 5xxs for affected tenants. This ticket captures the follow-up plan: implement a lightweight request-shaping proxy, add deferred prefetch probes, and introduce an early-KV-prune heuristic to reduce amplification and stabilize admission decisions.

Observed behavior and root cause hypotheses: 
- Sudden increase in concurrent long-context generation requests caused KV cache bloat and increased GPU memory pressure, increasing per-request processing time and reducing throughput.
- Autoscaler reacted with conservative downscales and then aggressive preemption; combined with admission bursts this produced a feedback loop where queues amplified faster than pools could recover.
- Our admission controller currently uses a per-pool token bucket without tenant-aware hints; tenants that run many warm-up prefetches amplified queueing.
- Prefetch/priming requests are indistinguishable from production traffic in admission scoring, which leads to non-linear admission collapse under mixed workloads.

Impact: High. Affected ~12% of hosted customers in the NA region for ~45 minutes, with visible application errors and degraded UX for several PLG customers.

Goals: 
1) Reduce amplification by avoiding wasteful prefetch work during capacity pressure.
2) Smooth admissions to avoid abrupt queue growth that triggers flapping autoscaling.
3) Provide an operational playbook that SRE and on-call can run to de-escalate and stabilize pools quickly.

Design overview: 
- Request shaper proxy: lightweight ingress-side component that applies short-term smoothing per-tenant and per-route. It will: (a) coalesce identical prefetch requests arriving within a 50–200ms window, (b) apply a soft ramp (token-hint) instead of immediate admission rejections, and (c) surface a rate-hint header to the admission controller to prefer best-effort handling for prefetches.
- Deferred prefetch probe: convert non-blocking prefetches into a background probe queue that runs at lower scheduling priority and is only executed when pool utilization < 70%. Probe requests will be tagged to ensure they are skipped by KV warm-up logic if capacity is constrained.
- Early KV prune heuristic: on admission, if KV cache growth is above expected baseline for the tenant's recent traffic profile, proactively prune least-recently-used KV segments that are not referenced by active latency-critical requests. This reduces memory pressure spikes and shortens GC pauses in the runtime.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Under a synthetic mixed traffic test (50% production, 50% prefetch-heavy tenants) the 95th percentile queue length across test pools falls by >= 40% vs baseline and median tail latency for prod requests improves by >= 25%.
- No regressions in correctness: generation outputs for prod requests must match baseline model outputs within existing fuzz thresholds.
- Playbook documented and validated by on-call during a simulated capacity event in the next chaos window.

Testing plan: 
- Unit tests for shaper logic and token-hint headers.
- Integration tests with admission controller in staging (runtime-1.23) with a traffic generator reproducing real tenant patterns.
- Chaos test: introduce transient GPU pressure and validate that the shaper + deferred prefetch reduces admission spikes and avoids autoscaler flapping.

Operational playbook (summary): 
1) Flip shaper to aggressive mode (config toggle) to enforce 200ms coalescing and 50% prefetch suppression.
2) Enable deferred-probe gating at pool-level; set probe threshold to 70%.
3) Temporarily increase admission timeout to allow in-flight coalescing to complete (avoid transient 429s).
4) If pools are still degrading, apply temporary tenant rate limits for top 5 contributing tenants and open incident Runbook step 3 for capacity expansion.

Rollback criteria: if we observe >5% increase in prod request errors or deviations in outputs outside eval thresholds after enabling components, roll back the shaper and deferred probe flags immediately and open a high-priority rollback PR.

Notes and links: Confluence playbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/HOST/Deferred-Prefetch-Playbook; Staging PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1248; Load test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hosted-gpu/queue-shaper-test.
